slides.title: Salbutamol
slides.subtitle: Albuterol
slides.highlight: Tachycardia, tremor; frequent doses can cause hypokalaemia: monitor K+
slides.moa: Stimulates β2 receptors, raising cAMP to relax bronchial smooth muscle: fast bronchodilation.
doses: MDI (with spacer): 2 puffs Q4-6 hrly PRN
Neb <4 yr: 0.63-2.5 mg/dose Q4-6 hrly PRN
Neb 5-11 yr: 1.25-5 mg/dose Q4-6 hrly; ≥12 yr: 2.5-5 mg/dose Q4-8 hrly

caption:
The most-used reliever in every paediatric emergency 💨 Salbutamol!

A short-acting β2 agonist that opens up the airways within minutes.
MDI with a spacer works as well as a nebuliser for most children.
In acute attacks it may be given more often: then watch heart rate and potassium.
